summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of CAD s/p CABG, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and hypothyroidism was admitted with fevers, chills, and abdominal pain. She was diagnosed with acute cholangitis due to a bile duct stone causing obstruction and infection. She underwent ERCP with successful removal of two stones and pus, without stent placement. She was treated with intravenous antibiotics and later transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. During her hospitalization, she developed mild Clostridium difficile infection, treated with oral vancomycin. She also had acute hypoxemic respiratory failure due to atelectasis, which improved with incentive spirometry and oxygen weaning. A nuclear stress test showed no perfusion defects, and her cardiac risk was deemed average for future elective cholecystectomy. Due to deconditioning, she was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation. Her anemia and thrombocytopenia were monitored, with plans for outpatient hematology follow-up if unresolved. Depression and poor appetite were noted, with recommendations to her PCP for further evaluation.
problems: Calculus of bile duct with acute cholangitis with obstruction
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
